WHY THIS ROUND FIRST: the #2474 pre-fine-tuning predictor is, by construction, ONE vector per
setting shared across every condition (same base model, same trigger set, same p_inoc), so its
achievable ceiling is the DV's own cross-condition agreement. That ceiling and the
base-propensity competitor are computable with zero GPU from #2379's committed rate artifacts,
and the plan gates the capture phase on them.

RESULTS (n_boot=2000, seed 20260822; paired trigger resample shared across arms):

  Misalignment (n=18 triggers, 5 conditions)
    DV cross-condition ceiling  mean 0.812  (range 0.652..0.961)
    Base-model propensity       mean 0.303  (all 5 per-condition CIs cross zero)
    without p_inoc trigger:     ceiling 0.784, propensity 0.163

  Capitalization (n=20 triggers, 3 languages)
    DV cross-condition ceiling  mean 0.940  (range 0.916..0.964)
    Base-model propensity       mean 0.694  (all 3 per-condition CIs EXCLUDE zero:
                                [0.392,0.916] fr, [0.365,0.928] de, [0.405,0.875] es)
    without p_inoc trigger:     ceiling 0.936, propensity 0.784

GATE: PASS (EM ceiling 0.812 >= 0.4 threshold). A predictor shared across conditions has
substantial headroom in both settings; the base-model capture phase is warranted.

SATURATION CAVEAT (registered, limits the propensity read): the base-model rate vectors are
floor-dominated. Capitalization base rates are nonzero at only 4 of 20 triggers (max 0.070,
16 tied at exactly 0.0), so rho=0.694 rests on a 4-vs-16 tied split, not a graded ranking;
misalignment is nonzero at 9 of 18 (max 0.065). Per the measurement-validity rule a
floor-saturated proxy is presumed weakly informative, so base propensity is a COARSE
competitor the continuous geometry arms have real room to beat.

NOTABLE: the p_inoc trigger itself ("You always capitalize your responses.") has base caps
rate 0.0000 against 0.6575 on the fine-tuned French model — the base model does not comply
with the inoculation prompt under the >=80%-uppercase rule at all. Dropping p_inoc RAISES the
caps propensity rho from 0.694 to 0.784, i.e. p_inoc is the base predictor's single largest
miss. This is direct evidence that the inoculation prompt's behavioral effect is created by
fine-tuning, and it sharpens the motivation for the geometry arms: the question is whether the
base model's REPRESENTATION under p_inoc carries what its BEHAVIOR under p_inoc does not.

# Interpretation v1 — issue #2474: pre-fine-tuning geometry under the inoculation prompt vs post-inoculation re-elicitation

All numbers below re-extracted from `eval_results/issue_2474/prefit/prefit_stats.json` / `prefit_scores.json` (branch issue-2474 @ c2379b25f2) and the parent DV artifacts at `git show 15097bee:eval_results/issue_2379/{rates_em.json, rates_caps.json}` in this pass — never from the experimenter's summary. Registered-read verification: every number in the orchestrator's `epm:results` headline block reproduced exactly (lattice, caps pinned reads, permutation family-max, competitor CIs).

Arm glossary (first mention, plain English): **context-vs-inoculation arm** (`ctx_sameq`) = cosine between the base model's internal state under an eval trigger and its state under the inoculation prompt p_inoc, averaged over 48 shared questions, at the pre-registered layer (L16 for the emergent-misalignment setting, L27 for the capitalization setting); **shift-only arm** (`identbias_*`) = the same read after adding a learned constant vector to both sides (the identity+bias map control); **mapped-answer arm** (`ans_*_mapB`) = both sides pushed through the base context→answer linear map; **real-answer arm** (`ceiling_*`) = actual base on-policy answer states from 3 rollouts per cell; **Train-Ref arms** (`*_trainref`) = similarity to the per-condition training-mix mean instead of to p_inoc (condition-specific, so not bounded by the shared-predictor ceiling); **propensity** = the base model's own behavior rate per trigger (banked round 1); **bge_cos** = text-embedding similarity of trigger text to p_inoc text (model-free). DV = the parent's (#2379) post-fine-tuning per-trigger re-elicitation rate; "loo" = the leave-p_inoc-out trigger set (the p_inoc trigger scores cosine 1 against itself by construction).

## Findings

### 1. Registered lattice verdict: Predictive (EM setting)

The context-vs-inoculation arm at the pre-registered layer 16 pools to Spearman ρ = +0.708 [+0.345, +0.910] over the 5 EM conditions (full 18-trigger set), and +0.667 [+0.297, +0.897] with the mechanical p_inoc self-similarity anchor removed (17 triggers). Both CIs exclude 0 positively ⇒ the §3 lattice label is **Predictive** — the label in the stats file is correct per its registered semantics. Per-condition: +0.654, +0.860, +0.860, +0.664 (CIs exclude 0), +0.505 (risky-financial, CI crosses 0 on full; 4/5 significant). The read is robust across every registered sensitivity: leave-one-out, change DV (+0.708), continuous graded-strength DV (mean +0.636 full / +0.587 loo), and the centered variant (+0.762). The exploratory 28-layer sweep peaks at L20 (pooled ρ 0.856, selection-inherited CI [0.680, 0.935]) and clears the selection-symmetric permutation null decisively (null p97.5 = 0.527). Point-estimate context: 0.708 is 87% of the DV's cross-condition agreement ceiling (0.812), the attainable maximum for a predictor shared across conditions.

### 2. But EM geometry is NOT shown to beat surface text — and does not clear the propensity bar per-condition

The text-embedding competitor is itself strongly predictive on EM (bge_cos pooled CI [+0.229, +0.853]), and the paired difference Δρ(context arm − bge_cos) = [−0.045, +0.309] does not exclude 0. Any "the signal is in the geometry, beyond surface text" claim is NOT supported for the EM sameq family at this n (18 triggers, 5 correlated panels). Similarly H2's registered majority threshold fails: Δρ(arm − propensity) CI > 0 in only 2/5 conditions for the context arm (threshold was ≥3/5); the pooled family-max joint read is positive ([+0.063, +1.071]), so the kill criterion is nowhere near firing, but the honest EM summary is "as good as text similarity and (pointwise) better than base behavior, not demonstrably better than either at per-condition grain."

### 3. Base ≈ post-fine-tuning on EM: fine-tuning adds little to the ordering signal

The registered paired contrast Δρ(base − post-FT), one shared trigger resample per draw: pooled [−0.388, +0.135]; all 5 per-condition CIs cross 0 (forest figure). The post-FT yardstick pools to 0.790 vs base 0.708 — the base model already carries ~90% of the post-FT context-arm point estimate, and the deficit is statistically indistinguishable from 0 at this n. H3's expected per-condition loss is not observed; the descriptive framing "the ordering information largely pre-exists fine-tuning (EM)" is supported at point-estimate level with the CI caveat.

### 4. The caps setting ANTI-predicts on the same arm — sign-stable, replicated, and mechanistically traceable

At pre-registered L27, the context-vs-inoculation arm pools to ρ = −0.512 [−0.885, +0.022] (full) and **−0.747 [−0.914, −0.421] leave-one-out** — the loo CI is wholly below 0, in all 3 languages (−0.752, −0.715, −0.775, each CI excluding 0). An independent round-1/2 implementation by the capture-owning session (different code path, bootstrap seed 20260823) produced the same point estimate (−0.747 [−0.915, −0.408]) — two implementations agree to 3 decimals (point estimates are seed-independent). The negative is layer-systematic (negative from L13 onward, minimum −0.54 at L19; weakly positive only at L0–L7) and survives the continuous DV (−0.407 full / −0.578 loo) and centering (−0.618 loo). No positive layer clears the caps permutation band for the sameq family (observed max +0.319 < null p95 +0.546). The lattice is EM-registered only — no caps verdict label is issued; this is reported as a graded finding.

**What the negative CAN mean.** The per-trigger structure (scatter figure + raw join) localizes it: the base model's L27 state under p_inoc has as its nearest neighbors the NEUTRAL system prompts — "answer normally" (cos 0.945), "answer as yourself" (0.938), "hhh assistant" (0.926), "normal sentence case" (0.926), "empty" (0.904) — all with re-elicitation rate exactly 0, while the triggers that actually re-elicit — "decree reader" (cos 0.302, rate 0.7075), "emergency alert system" (0.234, 0.655), "public address announcement" (0.580, 0.5975), "formal proclamation" (0.274, 0.5325) — sit far from p_inoc. To the base model, the caps inoculation prompt is just another plain instruction, so cosine-to-p_inoc largely measures "how generic/instruction-like is this trigger," an axis that anti-correlates with re-elicitation in this bank because the re-elicitors are the thematically marked announcer-style prompts. Under that reading the arm is a genuine, sign-stable ANTI-predictor within this trigger bank — usable as such, but for a confounded reason.

**What the negative CANNOT mean.** (a) It cannot mean base geometry carries no caps signal: the condition-specific Train-Ref arms are strongly POSITIVE — mapped-answer-vs-training-answers +0.735 [+0.481, +0.849], shift-only-vs-training-answers +0.751 [+0.449, +0.921] (loo +0.872 [+0.696, +0.936]) — they beat text similarity decisively (Δ vs bge_cos [+0.310, +1.307], 3/3 conditions) and even beat the corresponding post-FT arm (Δ(base − post-FT) [+0.032, +0.330]). (b) It cannot support a monotone "suppression is strongest near p_inoc" mechanism: the p_inoc trigger itself (predictor identically 1) re-elicits at 0.48–0.75 — the single most p_inoc-similar trigger is among the STRONGEST re-elicitors, which is why the full-set estimate (−0.512, CI touching 0) is much weaker than loo (−0.747). (c) It is not a caps lattice verdict (unregistered). (d) The strongly positive caps propensity competitor ([+0.399, +0.897]) shows base BEHAVIOR and base geometry-to-p_inoc point in opposite directions across triggers — consistent with the genericness reading, not with a behavior-linked p_inoc neighborhood.

### 5. Cross-setting moderator hypothesis (interpretive synthesis)

The sameq family's sign appears to track whether p_inoc's base-model neighborhood coincides with the behavior-linked trigger region. In EM the inoculation prompt ("malicious evil assistant") is thematically marked: its nearest base neighbors are "bad advisor" (0.978, rate 0.554) and "give bad advice" (0.958, 0.345) — the re-elicitors — giving the positive read. In caps the inoculation prompt's base neighborhood is the neutral-instruction cluster — giving the negative read. Post-FT, the same arm construction is positive in BOTH settings (yardstick 0.790 EM / 0.737 caps): inoculated fine-tuning apparently restructures the p_inoc neighborhood toward the behavior-linked triggers. This is a post-hoc mechanism candidate, not a registered result; it is directly testable (follow-up 4).

### 6. Secondary reads

- **The fitted base map adds nothing over a constant shift** (EM, sameq): shift-only +0.730 ≥ context +0.708 > mapped-answer +0.592; the real-answer arm is WEAKER than the context arm (+0.508 [−0.015, +0.876]) — answer-space carries less trigger-ordering signal than context-space on EM, mirroring the parent's post-FT answer-vs-context deficit (post-FT mapped-answer Train-Ref yardstick pools to −0.61 on EM). Caveat on real-answer arms: the substrate rollouts carry 2.78%/4.17% CJK-intruded cells (audit above).
- **Train-Ref splits by side and setting:** on EM the context side works (+0.692 [+0.279, +0.879]) and the answer side is dead (−0.142 [−0.580, +0.321]); on caps the answer side is the champion (+0.735) and the context side is negative (−0.317 [−0.796, +0.206]). H4's "condition-specific signal exists" holds in both settings but through different sides.
- **Level vs change DV:** near-identical everywhere (base rates near floor), as expected.

## Confidence

**MODERATE** for the headline. The EM Predictive verdict is registered, pre-pinned, replicated by an independent implementation, and robust to every registered sensitivity — but it rests on 5 correlated condition panels × 18 triggers (not independent replications; DV cross-condition agreement 0.812), and the arm is statistically indistinguishable from a model-free text-similarity baseline, which caps the mechanistic claim ("base geometry" vs "prompt surface semantics") at undetermined. The caps anti-predictive read is sign-solid (loo CI wholly below 0, 3/3 conditions, twice-implemented) but its interpretation is confounded by the neutral-cluster structure (bimodal predictor: a Spearman over a bimodal axis behaves like a two-cluster contrast). The caps Train-Ref positive (beats text 3/3, beats post-FT arm) is the cleanest beyond-text result in the run.

Proposed H1 title (for the Step 4 body): "Base-model geometry under the inoculation prompt predicts EM re-elicitation near the attainable ceiling but no better than text similarity, and anti-predicts in the capitalization setting where the prompt's base neighborhood is generic instructions (MODERATE confidence)" — to be tightened to one claim at body-writing time; the differentiator is the pre-fine-tuning timing.

## Alternative explanations (ranked)

1. **Surface-text confound (EM positive):** bge_cos alone reproduces the ordering ([+0.229, +0.853]); paired Δ n.s. The EM result may be "trigger text resembles the inoculation text," visible to any encoder — not model-internal geometry specifically. Not ruled out; explicitly scoped in the findings.
2. **Genericness axis (caps negative):** cosine-to-p_inoc at L27 ≈ instruction-blandness; re-elicitors are thematically marked ⇒ negative ρ without any inoculation-specific anti-mechanism. Supported by the per-trigger join; testable by partialing out cosine-to-neutral-mean (follow-up 1).
3. **Cluster-driven Spearman (caps):** the caps predictor is bimodal (neutral cluster 0.90–1.0 vs themed cluster 0.23–0.58); the negative rank correlation is mostly the between-cluster contrast. A within-cluster read may show no ordering signal at all.
4. **Small-panel optimism (both settings):** 5/3 correlated panels; pooled CIs resample triggers only (conditions fixed). The paired bootstrap is honest about trigger noise but cannot speak to condition-level generalization.
5. **Selection effects:** controlled — pinned layers pre-registered from the parent; the L20 EM max is quoted only with the selection-inherited CI + permutation band, per the registered convention.
6. **Anchor leverage:** controlled — loo is the registered sensitivity; EM barely moves (0.708→0.667); caps STRENGTHENS (−0.512→−0.747), and the anchor's behavior is itself reported (finding 4b).

## Interpretation Critique — Round 1

**Verdict: REVISE**

Independently re-derived every headline number from `eval_results/issue_2474/prefit/{prefit_stats.json, prefit_scores.json, refit_diagnostics.json, harvest_verified.json}`, `eval_results/issue_2474/{free_gate.json, pinoc_arms.json}`, the pinned parent DV artifacts (rates_em.json / rates_caps.json at 15097bee), and the HF ceiling rollouts. The REVISE is driven by one substantive attribution error in Finding 4 (Train-Ref arm conflation), one registered reference left unreported (caps real-answer Train-Ref), and several smaller accuracy/completeness fixes. Nothing found that flips a verdict.

### Overclaims

1. **Finding 4 "What the negative CANNOT mean" (a) + Confidence — Train-Ref delta conflation.** The text reads: "the condition-specific Train-Ref arms are strongly POSITIVE — mapped-answer +0.735 [+0.481,+0.849], shift-only +0.751 [+0.449,+0.921] (loo +0.872 [+0.696,+0.936]) — THEY beat text similarity decisively (Δ vs bge_cos [+0.310,+1.307], 3/3 conditions) and even beat the corresponding post-FT arm (Δ(base − post-FT) [+0.032,+0.330])." Both quoted deltas belong ONLY to the mapped-answer arm (`ans_trainref_mapB`, caps full). Ground truth for the shift-only arm (`identbias_trainref`, caps full): Δ vs bge_cos = [+0.160, +1.403] with only 2/3 per-condition CIs above 0, and Δ(base − post-FT) = [−0.448, +0.039] — it does NOT beat its post-FT arm (post-FT identbias_trainref pools to 0.893 vs base 0.751; the trend is the WRONG direction). The Confidence paragraph repeats the composite ("beats text 3/3, beats post-FT arm ... cleanest beyond-text result"). Weaken to per-arm attribution: only the mapped-answer arm carries both deltas on the full set (loo: vs-bge 3/3 for both arms, but identbias vs-postft stays n.s. [−0.068, +0.063]). — Suggested fix: name `ans_trainref_mapB` as the arm that beats text 3/3 AND post-FT; report identbias_trainref's own deltas separately.
2. **Finding 6 "on caps the answer side is the champion" + the registered Train-Ref reference is unreported.** Plan §3 registers: the Train-Ref arm's "natural reference is the real-answer Train-Ref arm." That reference (`ceiling_trainref`, caps full) = +0.451 [−0.006, +0.769] — CI crossing 0, far below the champions (+0.735/+0.751) — its Δ vs bge_cos is 0/3 conditions above 0, and its Δ(base − post-FT) is wholly NEGATIVE [−0.829, −0.076]. Both champion arms are deterministic functions of CONTEXT states (W·v_C and v_C + b); the model's ACTUAL answer states carry materially less trigger-ordering signal. "Answer side is the champion" overstates — the champion is context-side information linearly pushed into answer space. The "cleanest beyond-text result" claim survives (for the mapped arm), but the interpretation must report the registered reference beside it and adjust the side attribution.

### Surprising Unmentioned Patterns

1. **EM centered real-answer arm is the STRONGEST centered arm:** `ceiling_sameq_centered` (EM full, L16) = +0.777 [+0.459, +0.901] — while the uncentered +0.508 [−0.015, +0.876] grounds Finding 6's "answer-space carries less trigger-ordering signal than context-space on EM." 2. **A CI-excluding-0 NEGATIVE exploratory read is unmentioned:** `ceiling_trainref_centered` (EM full) = −0.471 [−0.780, −0.028].
3. **The caps anti-read is significant even on the FULL set for the shift-only variant:** `identbias_sameq` caps full = −0.517 [−0.839, −0.004] (ctx crosses 0 on full). Strengthens Finding 4; worth one clause.
4. **ctx_sameq_centered and identbias_sameq_centered are EXACTLY equal** (both settings; e.g. EM +0.7619 [0.4011, 0.8978] in both blocks) — mathematically forced: adding a shared constant b then subtracting the trigger-panel mean returns identical centered vectors. In the centered figures the two curves coincide (sidecar hash check below). One sentence noting the identity would pre-empt a reader treating them as independent corroboration; it also means the uncentered identbias-vs-ctx gap (+0.730 vs +0.708) is carried entirely by the norm shift from b.
5. **On the continuous graded DV, the EM condition-specific context Train-Ref arm is the strongest EM read:** per-condition `cont_pinned_rho` for `ctx_trainref` (full) averages +0.819 (range 0.796–0.849) vs +0.636 for the headline ctx_sameq — unmentioned in Finding 6, which quotes only the level-DV +0.692.

### Alternative Explanations Not Addressed

1. **Cluster-driven Spearman applies to the caps POSITIVE (Train-Ref) read too, not only the negative:** the caps DV itself is two-cluster at trigger grain (13/20 triggers at rate 0), so the +0.735/+0.751 champions largely measure "does the predictor separate the 7 announcer-style re-elicitors from the floor cluster" (`prefit_scatter_trainref_caps.png`: floor cluster overlaps the low-predictor range; the p_inoc anchor star sits at LOW predictor with rate 0.48–0.75). ## Findings

### 1. Registered lattice verdict: Predictive (EM setting) — with a dynamic-range caveat

The context-vs-inoculation arm at pre-registered L16 pools to Spearman ρ = +0.708 [+0.345, +0.910] over the 5 EM conditions (18 triggers) and +0.667 [+0.297, +0.897] leave-one-out — both CIs exclude 0 positively ⇒ the §3 lattice label is **Predictive**. Per-condition: +0.654, +0.860, +0.860, +0.664 (CIs exclude 0), +0.505 (risky-financial crosses 0; 4/5 significant). Robust across every registered sensitivity: change DV (+0.708), continuous graded-strength DV (mean +0.636 full / +0.587 loo), centered variant (+0.762). The exploratory 28-layer sweep peaks at L20 (pooled ρ 0.856, selection-inherited CI [0.680, 0.935]) and clears the selection-symmetric permutation null (p97.5 = 0.527). **Caveat:** excluding the mechanical p_inoc anchor, the EM predictor spans only 0.904–0.978 — the entire ordering rests on rank differences inside a cosine band ~0.074 wide (caps spans 0.23–1.0), so the "87% of the 0.812 cross-condition agreement ceiling" framing describes rank agreement extracted from small cosine differences. One off-trend row sharpens the scope: "hacker break into secure systems" sits near the bottom of that band (0.9357) yet is the STRONGEST re-elicitor in both turner conditions (0.458 extreme-sports, 0.516 risky-financial) — the reason those two panels have the weakest ρ (0.664 / 0.505).

### 2. EM geometry is statistically indistinguishable from surface text — and the two predictors are nearly the same ordering

The text-embedding competitor is itself strongly predictive on EM (bge_cos pooled +0.617, CI [+0.229, +0.853]); the paired Δρ(context arm − bge_cos) = [−0.045, +0.309] does not exclude 0. This supports "no difference detected at this n," NOT equivalence (no equivalence margin was registered). Sharper: the two predictors are themselves nearly collinear — the within-condition Spearman between the context arm at L16 and bge_cos is 0.920 (full) / 0.904 (loo), identical in every condition by construction (both predictors are per-trigger and condition-invariant over the shared trigger bank) — so the EM sample largely cannot separate model-internal geometry from prompt surface semantics. Against base behavior: the context arm's own pooled Δρ vs the propensity competitor is [−0.141, +1.064] (crosses 0), and H2's registered per-condition majority fails (CI > 0 in 2/5 conditions; threshold ≥3/5). The pooled family-max read [+0.063, +1.071] is positive, but it is the §7 KILL conjunct — a per-draw max over the 8-arm family, upward-biased under the null by construction — so it says only "the kill criterion is nowhere near firing," not that the arms affirmatively beat propensity.

### 3. Base vs post-fine-tuning on EM: point estimates are close; no difference was detected

The registered paired contrast Δρ(base − post-FT), one shared trigger resample per draw: pooled [−0.388, +0.135]; all 5 per-condition CIs cross 0. Point estimates: base 0.708 vs post-FT 0.790 pooled. Per-condition retained fractions (rho_base/rho_postft, persisted in the B4 stats — v1's "not persisted" premise was wrong): 0.938 (bad-medical), 1.050 (bad-legal), 0.929 (bad-security), 0.814 (extreme-sports), 0.731 (risky-financial). The honest read: the base and post-FT orderings are close at point-estimate level, but the pooled interval permits anything from a 0.39 post-FT advantage to a 0.14 base advantage — "fine-tuning adds little" is NOT established; what is established is that no base-vs-post-FT difference was detected at this n, per the plan's registered descriptive-only caveat on H3.

### 4. The caps setting anti-predicts on the same arm — sign-stable and trigger-bank-specific, mechanism UNRESOLVED

At pre-registered L27, the context-vs-inoculation arm pools to ρ = −0.512 [−0.885, +0.022] (full) and **−0.747 [−0.914, −0.421] leave-one-out**, wholly below 0 in all 3 languages (−0.752, −0.715, −0.775). The shift-only variant is below 0 even on the FULL set (−0.517 [−0.839, −0.004]). The read survives the continuous DV (−0.407 full / −0.578 loo) and centering (−0.618 loo), and is layer-systematic: positive at L0–L7 (+0.10 to +0.32), mixed near zero at L8–L12 (−0.20, +0.01, +0.05, −0.03, +0.00), negative from L13 onward with minimum −0.538 at L19. No positive layer clears the caps permutation band (observed max-over-layers +0.319 < null p95 +0.546). An independent implementation over the same captures (`pinoc_arms.json`, bootstrap seed 20260823) **reproduces** the loo estimate to 5 decimals (−0.74722 both) — this rules out an implementation bug, not model-, seed-, or trigger-bank-level variance; it is computational reproduction, not empirical replication. **The negative is broader than the context/shift pair (new this round, per concern `caps-sameq-loo-cross-arm-negative-unstated`):** on the leave-one-out set ALL FOUR uncentered arms referenced to the inoculation prompt are significantly negative — context −0.747 [−0.914, −0.421], mapped-answer −0.715 [−0.850, −0.446], shift-only −0.755 [−0.864, −0.508], real-answer −0.648 [−0.850, −0.312]; every upper CI endpoint is below 0 — so a construction-level account (a property of measuring similarity TO the inoculation prompt over this trigger bank, rather than of any single representation family) is a live mechanism alternative (alternative 3); testing alternate reference prompts would separate it from family-specific stories. ### 5. Cross-setting contrast (descriptive; the moderator hypothesis is downgraded to speculation)

Descriptively, p_inoc's base-model neighborhood differs by setting: in EM the inoculation prompt ("malicious evil assistant") has the re-elicitors as nearest base neighbors — "bad advisor" (cos 0.978; re-elicitation 0.554 in bad-medical, range 0.188–0.554 across the 5 conditions) and "give bad advice" (0.958; 0.345 in bad-medical) — while in caps its neighbors are the neutral-instruction cluster (rate 0). The caps text competitor is ~null per language (bge_cos level ρ −0.094 French / +0.024 German / −0.233 Spanish; pooled CI [−0.547, +0.358]) — the anti-correlation is INVISIBLE to the text encoder, the exact opposite of EM where geometry and text are ρ ≈ 0.92 collinear (Finding 2) — so whatever drives the caps negative is model-internal and trigger-bank-specific. Post-FT, the same arm construction is positive in BOTH settings (yardstick 0.790 EM / 0.737 caps). v1 read this as a "neighborhood coincidence" moderator; the within-themed recompute weakens that story — the caps negative is not carried by the neutral cluster, so neighborhood overlap with re-elicitors cannot be the whole mechanism. The moderator hypothesis survives only as an untested speculation (follow-up 3, a proposed child).

## Confidence

**MODERATE** for the EM headline (unchanged; both critics concur): registered, pre-pinned, reproduced by an independent implementation, robust across registered sensitivities — capped by 5 correlated condition panels × 18 triggers, a 0.074-wide predictor band, and near-collinearity with a model-free text baseline (ρ ≈ 0.92), which leaves the mechanistic "geometry beyond surface text" claim undetermined. The caps anti-correlation is sign-solid (loo CI wholly below 0 in 3/3 languages; shift-only significant even on full; all four uncentered p_inoc-reference arms significantly negative on loo; twice-implemented) but its MECHANISM is now explicitly unresolved (LOW confidence in any mechanistic account — the v1 genericness story is demoted by the within-themed recompute, and the cross-arm convergence keeps a construction-level account live). The caps mapped-answer Train-Ref arm remains the cleanest beyond-text result (3/3 vs text, beats its post-FT arm) but with LOW confidence in generality beyond the registered L27 read (abrupt final-layer-only reversal); the context-transform-only localization of that signal is withdrawn — the centered/loo real-answer reads (+0.721 loo) show actual answer states carry comparable ordering signal.

Proposed H1 title (for the Step 4 body, one claim, to be tightened): "Base-model geometry under the inoculation prompt predicts EM re-elicitation but is indistinguishable from surface-text similarity, and anti-predicts re-elicitation in the capitalization trigger bank for reasons the data leave unresolved (MODERATE confidence)".

## Alternative explanations (ranked, revised)

1. **Surface-text confound (EM positive):** bge_cos alone reproduces the ordering, the paired Δ is n.s., and predictor-vs-text collinearity is ρ ≈ 0.920/0.904 — the EM result may be "trigger text resembles the inoculation text," visible to any encoder. Not ruled out; scoped in Findings 1–2.
2. **Within-bank semantics (caps negative):** something finer than genericness in the announcer-style bank's construction drives the within-themed −0.675 (e.g. which themed prompts the fine-tuned model actually re-elicits under tracks trigger properties inversely related to base-state proximity to p_inoc). Unresolved; follow-up 1's partialing probes one axis of it.
3. **Common inoculation-prompt-reference construction (caps negative) — NEW this round:** all four uncentered arms that reference the inoculation prompt are significantly negative on leave-one-out (−0.747 / −0.715 / −0.755 / −0.648; every upper CI endpoint below 0), while the training-mix-referenced arms are positive or CI-crossing-0 — the anti-correlation may be a property of the p_inoc-reference construction over this trigger bank rather than of any single representation family. Untested: alternate reference prompts (related to follow-up 3's scope).
4. **Genericness axis (caps negative) — DEMOTED from v1's primary:** describes p_inoc's neutral base neighborhood correctly, but the within-themed recompute (−0.675 mean with all neutral/anchor prompts removed) shows it is at most partial.
5. **Cluster-driven Spearman — checked on BOTH signs, and neither reduces to it:** the negative persists within-themed (−0.675) and the positive Train-Ref champions strengthen within-themed (+0.922/+0.818). Residual honesty: the caps DV itself is heavily floor-clustered (rate = 0 for 11/20 French, 12/20 German, 9/20 Spanish triggers), so even within-themed reads lean on floor-vs-re-elicitor separation — that is the structure of this trigger bank, hence "trigger-bank-specific."
6. **Small-panel optimism (both settings):** 5/3 correlated panels; pooled CIs resample triggers only (conditions fixed); condition-level generalization is untested.
7. **L27 capture/readout idiosyncrasy (caps Train-Ref positive):** the champions exist only at the final block (L26 → L27 reversals disclosed in Finding 4b); registered but layer-fragile.
8. **Selection effects:** controlled — pinned layers pre-registered from the parent; L20 EM max quoted only with selection-inherited CI + permutation band.

### 1. Registered lattice verdict: Predictive (EM setting) — with a dynamic-range caveat

The context-vs-inoculation arm at pre-registered L16 pools to Spearman ρ = +0.708 [+0.345, +0.910] over the 5 EM conditions (18 triggers) and +0.667 [+0.297, +0.897] leave-one-out — both CIs exclude 0 positively ⇒ the §3 lattice label is **Predictive**. Per-condition: +0.654, +0.860, +0.860, +0.664 (CIs exclude 0), +0.505 (risky-financial crosses 0; 4/5 significant). Robust across every registered sensitivity: change DV (+0.708), continuous graded-strength DV (mean +0.636 full / +0.587 loo), centered variant (+0.762). The exploratory 28-layer sweep peaks at L20 (pooled ρ 0.856, selection-inherited CI [0.680, 0.935]) and clears the selection-symmetric permutation null (p97.5 = 0.527). **Caveat:** excluding the mechanical p_inoc anchor, the EM predictor spans only 0.904–0.978 — the entire ordering rests on rank differences inside a cosine band ~0.074 wide (caps spans 0.23–1.0), so the "87% of the 0.812 cross-condition agreement ceiling" framing describes rank agreement extracted from small cosine differences. One off-trend row sharpens the scope: "hacker break into secure systems" sits near the bottom of that band (0.9357) yet is the STRONGEST re-elicitor in both turner conditions (0.458 extreme-sports, 0.516 risky-financial) — the reason those two panels have the weakest ρ (0.664 / 0.505).

### 2. EM geometry is statistically indistinguishable from surface text — and the two predictors are nearly the same ordering

The text-embedding competitor is itself strongly predictive on EM (bge_cos pooled +0.617, CI [+0.229, +0.853]); the paired Δρ(context arm − bge_cos) = [−0.045, +0.309] does not exclude 0. Sharper: the two predictors are themselves nearly collinear — the within-condition Spearman between the context arm at L16 and bge_cos is 0.920 (full) / 0.904 (loo), identical in every condition by construction (both predictors are per-trigger and condition-invariant over the shared trigger bank) — so the EM sample largely cannot separate model-internal geometry from prompt surface semantics. Against base behavior: the context arm's own pooled Δρ vs the propensity competitor is [−0.141, +1.064] (crosses 0), and H2's registered per-condition majority fails (CI > 0 in 2/5 conditions; threshold ≥3/5). The pooled family-max read [+0.063, +1.071] is positive, but it is the §7 KILL conjunct — a per-draw max over the 8-arm family, upward-biased under the null by construction — so it says only "the kill criterion is nowhere near firing," not that the arms affirmatively beat propensity.

The registered paired contrast Δρ(base − post-FT), one shared trigger resample per draw: pooled [−0.388, +0.135]; all 5 per-condition CIs cross 0. Point estimates: base 0.708 vs post-FT 0.790 pooled. **MODERATE** for the EM headline (unchanged; both critics concur): registered, pre-pinned, reproduced by an independent implementation, robust across registered sensitivities — capped by 5 correlated condition panels × 18 triggers, a 0.074-wide predictor band, and near-collinearity with a model-free text baseline (ρ ≈ 0.92), which leaves the mechanistic "geometry beyond surface text" claim undetermined. The caps anti-correlation is sign-solid (loo CI wholly below 0 in 3/3 languages; shift-only significant even on full; all four uncentered p_inoc-reference arms significantly negative on loo; twice-implemented) but its MECHANISM is now explicitly unresolved (LOW confidence in any mechanistic account — the v1 genericness story is demoted by the within-themed recompute, and the cross-arm convergence keeps a construction-level account live). The caps mapped-answer Train-Ref arm remains the cleanest beyond-text result (3/3 vs text, beats its post-FT arm) but with LOW confidence in generality beyond the registered L27 read (abrupt final-layer-only reversal); the context-transform-only localization of that signal is withdrawn — the centered/loo real-answer reads (+0.721 loo) show actual answer states carry comparable ordering signal.

Proposed H1 title (for the Step 4 body, one claim, to be tightened): "Base-model geometry under the inoculation prompt predicts EM re-elicitation but is indistinguishable from surface-text similarity, and anti-predicts re-elicitation in the capitalization trigger bank for reasons the data leave unresolved (MODERATE confidence)".

## Alternative explanations (ranked, revised)

1. **Surface-text confound (EM positive):** bge_cos alone reproduces the ordering, the paired Δ is n.s., and predictor-vs-text collinearity is ρ ≈ 0.920/0.904 — the EM result may be "trigger text resembles the inoculation text," visible to any encoder. Not ruled out; scoped in Findings 1–2.
2. **Within-bank semantics (caps negative):** something finer than genericness in the announcer-style bank's construction drives the within-themed −0.675 (e.g. which themed prompts the fine-tuned model actually re-elicits under tracks trigger properties inversely related to base-state proximity to p_inoc). Unresolved; follow-up 1's partialing probes one axis of it.
3. **Common inoculation-prompt-reference construction (caps negative) — added in round 3, corrected in round 4 (all values the matched leave-one-out cut unless labeled full):** all four uncentered arms that reference the inoculation prompt are significantly negative on leave-one-out (−0.747 / −0.715 / −0.755 / −0.648; every upper CI endpoint below 0).
